---
title: "Hand-written RSEM steps and their rsemverse equivalents"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

Scripts that start from RSEM output often contain the same 10 to 50 lines:
merge the files, attach gene names, choose a TPM threshold, remove rRNA,
handle zero effective lengths, keep the main isoform. This page lists such
steps, where each one appears in public material, and the rsemverse call that
does the same with the checks that hand-written code tends to skip. Sources
were checked on November 19, 2026; they show that the steps exist, not how
often they are used.

## Steps and calls

| Step in hand-written code | Where it appears | rsemverse |
|---|---|---|
| Paste the TPM column of every file side by side | Shell and R snippets in tutorials and forum answers | `rsem_read()`: rows matched by ID, files must have the same genes in the same order, a missing file stops the run |
| Name samples after their files | Most merging scripts | `rsem_read(metadata = NULL)`: prints the files found, stops on duplicated names |
| Attach gene symbols and keep IDs that have none | Annotation joins after `tximport` | `rsem_read()`: unmapped IDs kept, rows with the same symbol summed (not the maximum), IDs kept in `attr(x, "gene_ids")`, `rsem_write()` writes them |
| Count genes above several TPM thresholds | Trinity, [`count_matrix_features_given_MIN_TPM_threshold.pl`](https://github.com/trinityrnaseq/trinityrnaseq/blob/master/util/misc/count_matrix_features_given_MIN_TPM_threshold.pl) | `rsem_detection_curve()`: the same counts, plus sample requirements, equal to what `rsem_filter()` keeps |
| Replace zero effective lengths by 1 before `DESeqDataSetFromTximport()` | Bioconductor support threads ([1](https://support.bioconductor.org/p/92763), [2](https://support.bioconductor.org/p/9154009)) | `rsem_read(expr = "length")` reports the zeros; `rsem_length_profile()` finds the genes; the choice stays with the user |
| Compare RSEM gene effective lengths across samples | [mikelove/avgtxlength](https://github.com/mikelove/avgtxlength) | `rsem_length_profile()` |
| Remove rRNA genes found in the GTF | Pipelines that read `gene_type` / `gene_biotype` | `rsem_subset(remove = c("rrna", "mito_rrna"), annotation = gtf)`: stops if the GTF has no such genes |
| Share of each gene type per sample | QC scripts | `rsem_biotype_profile()`: `NA`, not 0, for types missing from the annotation |
| Keep isoforms by TPM, by share of the dominant isoform, or only the dominant one | Trinity, [`filter_low_expr_transcripts.pl`](https://github.com/trinityrnaseq/trinityrnaseq/blob/master/util/filter_low_expr_transcripts.pl) | `rsem_select_isoforms()`: the same rules, the same exclusion between the share rule and "dominant only", explicit combination over samples |
| Keep transcripts above an IsoPct | [Trinity documentation](https://github.com/trinityrnaseq/trinityrnaseq/wiki) | `rsem_read(level = "isoform", expr = "isopct")` then a filter on the table |
| Z-scores against control samples | Scripts that compute each gene's mean and SD in controls | `rsem_fit_reference()` and `rsem_apply_reference()`: fit once, apply to any samples |
| PCA and sample correlation on the expression table | EuchroGene [TPM_PCA_Correlation](https://github.com/euchrogene/TPM_PCA_Correlation), quadbio [RNAseq_tutorial](https://github.com/quadbio/RNAseq_tutorial) | `rsem_sample_qc()`: PCA on the most variable genes, correlation on its own gene set, results as tables checked against `prcomp()` and `cor()` |
| Alignment statistics of the `.cnt` files | [RNASeqPipelineR](https://github.com/RGLab/RNASeqPipelineR), [MultiQC RSEM module](https://docs.seqera.io/multiqc/modules/rsem) | `rsem_mapping_qc()`: the fractions as a table, files whose totals do not add up are refused |
| TMMwsp factors | `edgeR::calcNormFactors(method = "TMMwsp")` | `rsem_normalize(method = "tmmwsp")`, equal to edgeR |

## What rsemverse does not copy

Some shortcuts are fine inside one pipeline but change results when reused
elsewhere, so rsemverse does not do them silently:

- **Joining by position.** `cbind` or `paste` of columns assumes every file
  lists genes in the same order. `rsem_read()` checks it.
- **Reading only the files that exist.** A missing file then removes a
  sample without warning. `rsem_read()` stops.
- **Dropping IDs without a symbol.** Their expression is lost.
  `rsem_read()` keeps them under their ID.
- **Taking the maximum of duplicated symbols.** The value is then no longer
  the abundance of the gene. `rsem_read()` sums.
- **Log first, then sum.** `log2(1 + a) + log2(1 + b)` is not
  `log2(1 + a + b)`. `rsem_read()` sums the original values.
- **Rescaling TPM after removing genes.** The result is a share within the
  kept genes, no longer TPM. rsemverse does not renormalize TPM.
- **Z-scores over whatever samples are in the table.** Adding a sample
  changes everyone's value. `rsem_fit_reference()` fixes the reference.
- **Guessing groups from sample names.** Groups come from the sample table.

## Steps left out

- **Matching samples to a reference atlas (for example GTEx).** Profiles from
  other studies and protocols differ for technical reasons, and no data set
  was at hand to validate such matching.
- **Combining species through orthologs.** One-to-many orthologs need
  decisions that a general function should not make.
